title: Review without reading the code
about: Every line of code in this film is read from examples/plugged-in, and every line of terminal output is replayed from docs/manual/captures, recorded by running the commands for real. The change was staged by the recording.

scenes.title: Someone who wrote none of it

lines.text: A change has come back. You asked for two small things about claiming a name: a plainer description, and a tighter time budget.
Nine files changed. You should not have to read nine files.
So the change goes to a reviewer: an agent that wrote none of it.
It is given two things. The change, and the brief the change was made from. Here, the brief is your two sentences.
It touches nothing. It reads, it runs commands, and it reports.
The reviewer starts with the blueprint's part of the change, because that is the part you will read.
Two lines out, two lines in. The description. And the budget: a hundred and fifty milliseconds becomes a hundred.
Then every file the change touched. One is the blueprint's. Eight are generated.
No handler. No journey. And nobody reads the eight: a check will say whether they are exactly what the blueprint makes.
Next: how far does the change reach? One command says: ortho impact.
It compares with the record the last full proof left on this machine. Before the change: nothing stale, and seven operations proven.
With the change in place, it names the declaration that changed: handle.claim, its budget and its description.
lines.say: With the change in place, it names the declaration that changed: handle dot claim, its budget and its description.

lines.text: And it names what that unproved. One operation is stale. The other six stand.
A report that says it passes is a claim. So the reviewer runs the whole proof itself.
Seven journeys pass. And claim's performance line is now measured against the new budget: a hundred milliseconds.
Then the check. Drift passes. That one line is why nobody read the eight generated files.
Ask impact once more. Nothing stale. Seven proven, as before the change.
You read four lines of blueprint, and the reviewer's findings. A finding names a file, a line, and what would make it right.
When a change arrives before generate was run, the check fails, and names every file that is behind.
When an operation goes stale and no line says what changed, the code moved and the blueprint did not. That is when the reviewer reads the handler.
And ask impact before you prove. A full proof writes a new record, and after it nothing is stale.
Honest notes. This was staged: the recording made the change, and no reviewer was filmed reading it. And no command checks who wrote what. That is practice.
Next: run the app, break it, and read the trace.

pictures.carries: The row of seven operations, each with its proof mark, counted from the impact recordings: all seven proven (review-impact-before), handle.claim alone stale (review-impact), all seven proven again (review-impact-after). It returns in the stale, prove and report sheets.
pictures.hand: Kit.who shows you handing the change to the reviewer; an editor quotes the two changed lines of examples/plugged-in/blueprint/things/handle/verbs/claim.ts as they stand before the change, and the count of nine files is read from the last line of review-stat.
pictures.read: A terminal replays review-diff (the blueprint's two lines out and two lines in), then review-stat, with the one blueprint row set apart from the eight generated rows; the counts one and eight are computed from review-stat.
pictures.stale: A terminal replays review-impact-before and then review-impact, and the row of seven operations is drawn from their stale and proven lines: seven proven, then handle.claim marked stale (not red: stale is not a verdict).
pictures.prove: A terminal replays review-prove (the seven journey lines, handle.claim's performance line with the budget of 100ms, and the last line), then review-check with its drift line, then review-impact-after; the row of seven returns to all proven.
pictures.report: Kit.who shows you reading; two small terminals replay review-check-early (drift failing on eight files) and review-impact-handler (stale handle.claim with no changed line above it); Kit.stand marks the commands as running today, the reviewer's independence and who wrote what as practice, and a printed brief for a blueprint change as missing, and says the change was staged by the recording.
